record.original_question: Let C be a simple planar convex curve contained in a plane P, let D be the planar domain bounded by C, and let Sigma be a compact constant-mean-curvature surface spanning C. If Sigma is contained in D x R, must Sigma be a graph on D?

evidence.quote: For example, suppose that C is a simple closed curve contained in a plane P and let D be the bounded domain by C in P.
Problem 3.6 (3*). Let C subset P be a simple planar convex curve. Let Sigma be a compact cmc surface spanning C. If Sigma is included in D x R, is Sigma a graph on D?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a plane and let $C \subset P$ be a simple closed planar convex curve. Denote by $D \subset P$ the bounded planar domain enclosed by $C$. Identify $P$ with $\mathbb{R}^2$ and consider the vertical cylinder $D \times \mathbb{R} \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ (where the $\mathbb{R}$-direction is taken orthogonal to $P$). Let $\Sigma \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a compact, connected, embedded surface with constant mean curvature whose boundary is $C$ (i.e., $\Sigma$ spans $C$). Suppose that $\Sigma \subset \overline{D} \times \mathbb{R}$. Must $\Sigma$ be a graph over $D$, that is, must there exist a function $u: \overline{D} \to \mathbb{R}$ with $u|_C = 0$ such that $\Sigma = \{(x, u(x)) : x \in \overline{D}\}$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem about whether confinement of a compact CMC surface to the vertical cylinder over a convex planar domain forces it to be a graph. Web search did not return a published resolution; related results (e.g., for circular boundaries via Hoffman–Rosenberg–Spruck, and graph results assuming additional hypotheses) do not settle the general convex case.

status_evidence.title: Surfaces with constant mean curvature in Euclidean space (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of CMC surfaces with boundary discussing graph and confinement-type problems.
status_evidence.claim: Related graph/confinement problems for CMC surfaces with planar boundary are discussed but the convex-cylinder version is not resolved there.

status_evidence.title: Compact constant mean curvature surfaces in Euclidean three-space
status_evidence.snippet: Studies compact CMC surfaces with planar boundary, including graph-type conclusions under symmetry or circular boundary hypotheses.
status_evidence.claim: Graph conclusions are known under stronger hypotheses (circular boundary), but the general convex case under cylinder confinement is not established.
